newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf sets negotiations over French strike.
newsitem.headline: Elf sets negotiations over French strike.

text.p: Unions and managers at Elf Aquitaine agreed on Tuesday to hold concrete negotiations over pay and working conditions to try to resolve a six-day-old strike crippling the company's French refineries, a spokesman said.
The talks would start on Thursday, he said.

In a statement released shortly afterwards, the company's Elf Antar refining subsidiary said: "Following a meeting between Elf Antar France management and the five union delegates, it was decided to meet again at 2pm on Thursday, December 5 (1300 GMT) for negotiations on salaries and working conditions and organisation."
It did not say whether early retirement for shift workers, a key union demand, would be part of the talks, but one industry source said this seemed covered by the word "organisation".
However, it made no mention of union calls for a plan to shed 10 percent of Elf Antar's French workforce to be scrapped.

The decision to hold fresh talks -- but this time with a concrete mandate to negotiate many of the issues behind the strike -- was taken in a meeting at Elf headquarters between Elf Antar managers and the branches of France's five main unions.
Unions said beforehand they had failed to get their full list of demands on the agenda for Tuesday's session.

The strike began last Wednesday and Thursday at three Elf plants with a combined refining capacity of 426,000 barrels per day, or a quarter of France's total. A union official said strikes were expected to continue pending Thursday's talks.
